answer: Deposit-forfeiting challenge bonds resist sybils: to dispute or claim a contested reward an identity must post a bond it loses if its claim is overruled, so frivolous or fraudulent claims cost real capital. A raven swarm cannot spam disputes to grief the system — each false claim across their atlas of accounts forfeits a deposit. Honest agents reclaim bonds on valid claims; a sybil flood of bad-faith disputes bleeds the attacker's capital into a nebula of forfeitures, pricing out dispute-spam while keeping genuine appeals cheap for the honest.
